editorial:
Imagine sitting down with a creepy old man who knows all the dark secrets of his small town. That is exactly how you start this ride. You follow a reporter who listens to an uncle tell four different scary stories about a place called Oldfield. The vibe is like a campfire ghost story session where each tale gets weirder than the last. You get everything from a man who loves a woman too much to a group of kids who are way more dangerous than they look. It feels like a twisted anthology book come to life, and it keeps you guessing about what will happen next in each tiny story.

The acting is solid and the special effects have a cool old-school feel that you just do not see anymore. While some parts move a bit slow, the twists in the stories make up for it. If you love weird stories that do not follow the rules, you will really enjoy this one. It is a great pick for a rainy Friday night. You should look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or you can try renting it on Apple TV to see if it is your thing.
endingExplained: The final story wraps up with the soldiers realizing the orphans are not innocent kids, but monsters who want to use them. After the horror unfolds, the movie circles back to the reporter and the uncle. You find out that the uncle is not just telling stories for fun. He is connected to the town's dark history, and the whole experience leaves you feeling like the evil in Oldfield is still alive and waiting.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school horror stories and twist endings.
